name: Truck and bus crashes by county, state and year (FMCSA crash file)
description: Crashes involving a commercial truck or bus that states reported to the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), counted from its Motor Carrier Management Information System (MCMIS) crash file for every county, state and territory and the US over the last ten complete calendar years. Each record gives, for the latest year, the crashes, the fatal crashes, the crashes with injuries, the crashes where a vehicle was towed away, the crashes involving a bus, the deaths and the injuries, with the whole ten-year history and the ten-year totals. A crash is one state crash report, counted once however many trucks and buses it involved, and its deaths and injuries are counted once. State records add the number of active carriers based in the state, from the FMCSA Company Census File. Counties with no reported crash are listed with zeros, and reports without a usable county code are kept in a 'county not given' row for their state, so counties always add up to the state.
citeAs: Probative Growth. (2026). Truck and bus crashes by county, state and year (FMCSA crash file) (Version 2.0.1) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24116060

distribution.name: truck-crashes.csv
distribution.description: Every record, one row each (RFC 4180, UTF-8). Columns are described in README.txt.

distribution.name: truck-crashes.json
distribution.description: Every record with its full sources, under a meta envelope (credit line, DOI, license).

distribution.name: truck-crashes-values.csv
distribution.description: The columns listed in README.txt as being in truck-crashes-values.csv, one row per id, column and value; join it to truck-crashes.csv on id.

recordSet.name: truck-crashes
recordSet.description: The records of Truck and bus crashes by county, state and year (FMCSA crash file), one per CSV row.

field.name: id
field.description: Stable record id (never reused)

field.name: jurisdiction
field.description: Two-letter code of the state or territory the crash happened in, or US

field.name: level
field.description: county, county-not-given (reports in the state without a usable county code), state, state-not-given (reports without a U.S. state code) or us

field.name: year
field.description: The latest complete calendar year in the record (the others are under `years` in the JSON)

field.name: status
field.description: P primary source, S secondary source

field.name: text
field.description: The record in one plain-English sentence

field.name: value
field.description: Crashes in that year (same as crashes)

field.name: unit
field.description: Unit of value

field.name: crashes
field.description: Federally reportable crashes involving at least one truck or bus, counted once per state crash report

field.name: fatal_crashes
field.description: Crashes in which someone died

field.name: injury_crashes
field.description: Crashes in which someone was injured

field.name: towaway_crashes
field.description: Crashes in which a vehicle was towed away because of damage

field.name: bus_crashes
field.description: Crashes involving at least one bus

field.name: deaths
field.description: People killed in those crashes (anyone: truck or bus occupants, other drivers, pedestrians), counted once per crash

field.name: injuries
field.description: People injured in those crashes, counted once per crash

field.name: crashes_10y
field.description: Crashes over the ten years in `years`

field.name: deaths_10y
field.description: Deaths over the ten years in `years`

field.name: effectiveFrom
field.description: When the fact took effect (YYYY-MM-DD), if known

field.name: effectiveTo
field.description: When it stopped applying; empty while current

field.name: lastChecked
field.description: The day it was last confirmed (YYYY-MM-DD)

field.name: sourceLabels
field.description: Sources, separated by " | "

field.name: sourceUrls
field.description: Source URLs, in the same order

field.name: confidence
field.description: high, medium or low: computed from status, a second check, age against the refresh cadence and sampling error (rule: /data/#confidence)

field.name: confidenceBasis
field.description: The reasons for the confidence level, in a short phrase
